topic.title: The friend who settles up in an hour
topic.claim: The friend who pays you back on UPI within an hour isn't being petty about money; they're telling you they don't want money between you.
topic.moment: Dinner ends, someone posts the split, and one friend has paid before the cab arrives.

turn.believed: Settling up fast means a person is fussy about money.
turn.actually: It's often the most generous habit in the group, because it protects the friendship.

topic.feeling: Relieved, and a little guilty about the ₹600 I still owe someone.
topic.villain: Small unpaid amounts that slowly turn into resentment.
topic.because: Small debts nobody mentions grow into quiet grudges. Paying fast removes the thing nobody wants to bring up.
topic.payoff: Check your UPI history. Who in your group has never made you ask twice? Keep them.
topic.behaviour: Friends split bills on apps or in chat, and some pay instantly while others wait for reminders.
topic.mechanism: Quick repayment removes awkwardness before it can grow.
topic.group: Friend groups in their 20s splitting dinners and trips
topic.send_to: The friend who always pays first, so they know someone noticed.
topic.why_now: Trips and dinners are split to the rupee now, so these habits are on display.

score.why: The warm side: the friend who pays back fast is protecting the friendship. Sendable to that exact friend.
